one_line_contribution: A retrieval-neighborhood-conditional leave-one-out estimator of a memory item's marginal utility inside the bundle it is actually injected in, plus a split-half accounting intended to split the gap between a screen's projected and realized gain into a winner's-curse component and an item-interference component.
closest_prior_work: Two lines, neither of which the proposal disposes of. (1) Per-example counterfactual valuation for in-context learning: influence-based selection (the cited Nguyen & Wong 2023) and the Shapley/LOO demonstration-valuation line more broadly already compute exactly y_full - y_{-m} style quantities per example and already screen on them. The proposal's increment is conditioning the average on the retrieval neighborhood rather than a global validation sample - a real but narrow increment, and one that survives only if P2 is actually established, which as designed it cannot be (see strongest_objection). (2) The statistical half is transplantation, not invention: winner's curse, Tweedie/EB shrinkage, and BH-FDR applied to selection on noisy per-unit estimates are textbook, and the closely analogous finding that prompt-optimizer / demonstration-set selection overfits its own validation scores is already circulating for MIPRO/GEPA-class optimizers. If that result exists in the 2025-26 preprint literature for prompt optimization (which the authors did not check), 'the same thing, one slot over, for memory items' is an incremental application. The RL memory-curation line (Memory-R1-style) is correctly identified as the dangerous neighbour but is then instantiated as a strawman (see missing_baseline).
strongest_objection: P4 is declared the load-bearing prediction and it is not identified. The screened bank is a *smaller bank*, so top-7 retrieval on held-out queries backfills items that ranked 8, 9, 10... in the unscreened bank. Those promoted items appear in deployed bundles whose composition was never probed, and their utility was estimated (if at all) in a different bundle. That effect lands entirely in the residual G_unbiased - G_actual, which P4 and its refutation clause read as 'non-additivity / interference among co-injected items'. Worse, the E4 discriminator fails: backfill does not shrink with probe budget m either, so the proposal's stated test ('winner's curse shrinks in m, non-additivity does not') cannot separate interference from re-retrieval composition change or from probe/test neighborhood shift. The paper would then report 'interference' for an artifact of deleting items from a ranked index. Second, and possibly fatal earlier in the pipeline: the per-item SNR. Utility observations are paired binary EM deltas in {-1,0,+1}; with a discordance rate of the 10-20% the proposal itself assumes and m = 12, SE(u_hat_i) is roughly sqrt(0.15/12) = 0.11, i.e. about 11 accuracy points, while any plausible true per-item marginal effect is a fraction of a point. u_hat_i is then essentially pure noise, and P1's requirement that split-half measured utility reach AUC >= 0.65 - the one signal that must beat the write-path signals for the paper to have a screen at all - is the bet the whole design rests on, and the arithmetic says it lands near 0.5. Third, P2's thresholds are calibrated below the noise-only null in the wrong direction: two independent noisy estimates of near-zero quantities disagree in sign roughly 40-50% of the time, so '>= 25% of items flip sign between global and neighborhood estimates' is confirmed by measurement noise with no neighborhood conditionality present at all; the same objection voids E3b's singleton-vs-LOO sign-flip rate and P6's rank-correlation >= 0.4. Relatedly, the mixed-effects claim that '>= 30% of explained variance' is item x neighborhood interaction is not estimable: with exactly one observation per (item, query) cell, the interaction variance component is aliased with the Bernoulli residual and is set by whatever the model assumes, not by the data.
what_would_fix_it: All the essential fixes are analysis-level and cost zero extra episodes, which is why this is borderline rather than reject. (1) Calibrate every sign-flip, correlation, and AUC statistic against a noise-only null built from the split-half data you already collect: report neighborhood A-vs-B sign disagreement as the floor, and claim P2 only if global-vs-neighborhood disagreement exceeds it; do the same for E3b and for P6's rank correlation. (2) Close the backfill hole: either freeze the retrieved bundle composition when evaluating the screened bank (evaluate B(q) minus removed items, at reduced k, so the estimand matches the estimator) or add a third split-half term that measures the utility of promoted items in their new bundles, and stop calling the residual 'interference' until backfill is subtracted. Reporting bank-size and bundle-overlap statistics between screened and unscreened deployment is the minimum. (3) Report the EB posterior distribution before committing: with m~12 and tiny per-item effects, tau^2 will be near zero and the P(u_i>0)>0.7 rule degenerates to keep-almost-all (if mu>0) or keep-almost-none (if mu<0, which the pilot's harmful bank predicts). In the second case the EB cell is mechanically a no-memory cell and the headline contrast is vacuous; the risk-factor pre-check catches an empty bank but not this degeneracy. (4) Re-probe under instruction B for at least a subset so E5 becomes an interaction contrast (screen-fit-on-A vs screen-fit-on-B, both evaluated under B) instead of a replication that cannot distinguish co-adaptation from B simply being harder. (5) Execute a real literature search before submission.
missing_baseline: An oracle / held-out-fit screen: fit the admission rule directly on the evaluation labels and report it as a ceiling cell. Without it, the very likely outcome (screened bank indistinguishable from no-memory) is uninterpretable - a reviewer cannot tell whether the bank simply contains no positive-utility items, whether item-level admission is the wrong granularity, or whether the probe budget is too small, and the proposal's headline negative result becomes unattributable. Two smaller omissions a reviewer would also name: EB-screened at k=3 (you compare EB@k=7 against unscreened@k=3, so screening and volume are never crossed at the same injection budget, and the random size/token-matched control does not substitute for that cell); and a bundle-level selector - greedy or submodular forward selection over bundles at the same 3,200-episode probe budget - which is the obvious competitor once interference is named as a candidate mechanism, and which the proposal relegates to a framing sentence ('screen bundles, not items') in P4's refutation clause. The bandit curator (baseline 8) does not fill this gap: Thompson sampling over a 240-arm keep/drop space with episode-level shared credit at 3,200 episodes (~13 episodes per item) is constructed to lose, and predicting that your paired estimator beats it is not informative about the RL-curation line it is standing in for.
preprint_collision: This is the weakest section of the submission and I judge it as a negative, not a neutral. The check reports zero executed searches - two consecutive rounds of tool failure - no titles, no dates, no CLOSEST/GAP table, and an explicitly 'unverified recollection' list. By the standard that novelty must be established rather than asserted, novelty here is simply not established, and the honesty about that (which I do credit for integrity) does not substitute for the search. The proposed mitigation - pre-emptively retargeting the headline to the selection-noise decomposition so a colliding screening preprint would not subsume the paper - is sensible risk management but it moves the novelty burden onto exactly the half that is the least novel in the abstract (winner's curse plus EB shrinkage is standard machinery) and the least identified in the design (see strongest_objection). The specific collisions I would want checked before I could support acceptance: 2025-26 arXiv work on validation overfitting / selection noise in prompt and demonstration optimizers (MIPRO/GEPA-class gains shrinking on true held-out sets), which is the same selection-on-noise claim in an adjacent setting; the 2025 agentic-memory curation line (ReasoningBank, Memory-R1, A-MEM/Mem0-style consolidation) for utility-based or reward-based admission; and Shapley/LOO demonstration-valuation preprints for retrieval-conditioned example scoring. The authors' own stated collision criterion (a preprint doing both neighborhood-conditional counterfactual utility and a split-sample transfer analysis) is drawn narrowly enough that it would clear almost anything; a reviewer will apply a looser one.
